{{Quote|I think, therefore I am. I destroy, therefore I endure.|[[IG-88A/Legends|IG-88A's]] final thoughts|<ref name="IG88 Tale" />}}
'''IG-88''', also known as the '''IG-series assassin droid''' or '''IG-series combat prototype''', was an [[Assassin droid/Legends|assassin droid]] line designed by [[Holowan Laboratories/Legends|Holowan Laboratories]]. The IG-88 line was a derivative of the [[IG-86 sentinel droid/Legends|IG-86 sentinel droids]] used during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]]. [[IG-88B/Legends|IG-88B]] later became one of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy's]] most infamous [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunters]]. However, the bounty hunting was just a cover for his master, [[IG-88A/Legends|IG-88A]], and his grand plan&mdash;the [[Droid Revolution]].

Moments after activation, the original massacred the scientists and transferred his consciousness into the other three. They then escaped the lab. It was possible it was the droid's incompletely formed identity that made him obsessed with bounty hunting and killing.<ref name="SWCVD">''[[Star Wars: The Complete Visual Dictionary]]''</ref>

==Biography==
{{Quote|WANTED: IG-88, aka the Phlutdroid, also reportedly operating as IG-88A, IG-88B, IG-88C, or IG-88D. Heavily armed, more than 150 kills. DISMANTLE ON SIGHT.|[[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] bounty posting|<ref name="The New Essential Guide to Droids">''[[The New Essential Guide to Droids]]''</ref>}}
===Design history===
{{Quote|The ''Techno Union'' are ''wealthy'', Snips. They're so used to having ''servants'' around&mdash;even if they're usually droids&mdash;that they won't ''pay attention'' to you. Which means ''no one'' will ''notice'' when you leave to explore the base and find those advanced ''battle droid plans'' we need.|[[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]], to [[Ahsoka Tano/Legends|Ahsoka Tano]]|<ref name="Suited">{{TCWComicCite|6.10|Suited}}</ref>}}[[File:Unidentified_Techno_Union_battle_droid.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Ahsoka Tano stealing the Techno Union’s plans for an advanced battle droid, later known as IG-88.]]
During the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], the [[Techno Union/Legends|Techno Union]] designed schematics for an advanced [[Battle droid/Legends|battle droid]]. [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] Anakin Skywalker and his [[Padawan/Legends|Padawan]] Ahsoka Tano undertook a [[Mission to unidentified Techno Union planet|mission]] to steal the plans from a Techno Union [[Unidentified Techno Union base|base]]. Skywalker posed as a [[Merchant/Legends|merchant]] named "Kwarelsky" while Ahsoka stole the advanced battle droid plans before resuming her master.<ref name="Suited" />

Assassin droids were banned even before the Empire came to power, although many beings continued to use them. The very nature of their job necessitated highly adaptive, autonomous programming that unfortunately caused them to frequently turn on their masters. The droid programmers at [[Holowan Laboratories/Legends|Holowan Laboratories]], however, developed new programming methods that they felt confident would keep their new line of assassin droids in check, even with their new sentience programming. Thus, the development of the IG-series assassin droids&mdash;also known as the [[Phlut Design Systems/Legends|Phlut Design Systems]] [[Project Phlutdroid/Legends|Project Phlutdroid]]&mdash;would become well known as an idea that went wrong with disastrous results. The droids were also similar to [[IG-72/Legends|IG-72]] and [[IG-97 battle droid|IG-97]], but the IG-88 line was by far the most infamous.

===Activation & awareness===
[[File:IG-88_activated.jpg|thumb|right|250px|The IG-88 droids are activated.]]
Evolving from Phlut's contract with the [[InterGalactic Banking Clan/Legends|InterGalactic Banking Clan]] (hence the "IG" prefix), IG-88 was a natural design evolution from the [[IG-100 MagnaGuard/Legends|IG-100 MagnaGuards]], [[IG-86 sentinel droid/Legends|IG-86 sentinel droids]] and [[IG lancer droid/Legends|IG lancer combat droids]] that had made their mark during the violent [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]]. Only four of these droids were ever created, and all were completely identical. While these creations were supposedly subservient to their masters, when IG-88 was activated, the sentience programming&mdash;designed to make the droid a more adaptive and resourceful assassin&mdash;had results far outstripping their expectations. Within a few seconds, he had chewed through the data files in the computer, realized he was an assassin droid, and reasoned his superiority to the biological creatures who had created him. The designers only had time to decide to deactivate the droid and find out why he was outperforming their expectations&mdash;which the droid decided he would not allow. He then proceeded to slaughter his makers with his bare hands, copy his programming into three other IG-88s, [[Death/Legends|kill]] the majority of the guards in the Holowan Labs complex, and escape. Before making his escape, he also freed the droid designated [[IG-72/Legends|IG-72]]. It should be noted that he did not copy himself over into IG-72's programming, as the latter droid expressed a desire to maintain its own individuality, whereas the other three droids had empty memory cores.<ref name="IG88 Tale" />

IG-88 designated himself as "A" and the rest in activation order "B, C, and D". They worked in tandem, while IG-72 went his own way. They traveled to [[Mechis III/Legends|Mechis III]] and conquered the droid factory there, killing all of its biological occupants. To throw Imperial investigators off their trail, IG-88B worked as a [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]], killing various former employees of Holowan to prevent discovery.<ref name="IG88 Tale" /> It was rumored that the IGs were intentionally programmed to kill their designers by an outside agency, most likely the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]].<ref name="Cynabar's Fantastic Technology">''[[Cynabar's Fantastic Technology: Droids]]''</ref>

===The droid revolution===
From their base on Mechis III, the four IG-88s began planning their "[[Droid Revolution]]," a movement in which an army of all types of droids would rise up and annihilate all the "biologicals" of the universe. After taking control of Mechis III, they began uploading their advanced sentience program into all droids manufactured there; the sentience programming was to be loaded into the droids when the appropriate code was sent by the IG-88s. When this occurred, all of the droids would rise up and destroy all biological lifeforms.<ref name="IG88 Tale" />

At some point around [[1 ABY/Legends|1 ABY]], IG-88 reactivated a [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]]-era [[Corellia Droid Factory|droid factory]] on Corellia. The former [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Separatist]] factory produced [[B1-series battle droid/Legends|B1-Series battle droids]], [[B2-series super battle droid/Legends|B2 super battle droids]] and [[Droideka/Legends|droidekas]] until it was shut down by the [[Corellian Security Force]].<ref name="SWG:DtDF">{{SWGcite|exp=NGE|type=class|Legacy|Disable the Droid Factory|Corellia}}</ref> Sometime later, IG-88A set up a [[Nym's Factory Compound|droid factory]] on [[Lok/Legends|Lok]] in replacement where he planned to manufacture a plethora of [[Battle droid/Legends|battle droids]] for his own nefarious purposes. However, with the help of [[Nym/Legends|Nym]], a group of [[Spacer/Legends|spacers]] were successful in foiling his plans and seemingly [[Battle of Nym's Factory Compound|destroying]] the droid and the factory.<ref name="SWG:C7">{{SWGcite|exp=NGE|type=other}}Chapter 7: A Collection of Heroes</ref>

===Bounty hunting===
[[File:IG-88-DTNK.jpg|thumb|left|250px|IG-88 hunting for [[Mon Julpa]]]]
{{Quote|Why do people keep hiring him? They're risking the wrath of the Empire.''"<br />"''Sir, I believe it's because IG-88 always gets the job done.|[[Gurdun]] and [[Minor Relsted]]|<ref name="IG88 Tale" />}}
The IG-88 designated "B" operated as a bounty hunter, with his appearances throughout the galaxy serving as cover for their real operations on Mechis III. One assignment saw the droid bounty hunter hired by [[Ko Zatec-Cha]], [[Vizier/Legends|vizier]] of [[Tammuz-an/Legends|Tammuz-an]], to track down the missing [[Prince/Legends|Prince]] [[Mon Julpa]]. IG-88 tracked Julpa to [[Tyne's Horky]] and followed him to see if the lost Prince would lead him to the [[Tammuz-an royal scepter|Tammuz-an Royal Scepter]]. During the course of this assignment, IG-88 would cross paths with the droids [[R2-D2/Legends|R2-D2]] and [[C-3PO/Legends|C-3PO]].<ref name="ANK">{{DroidsCite|The New King}}</ref>

[[File:ZuckussShot.jpg|thumb|right|250px|IG-88 during the quest for the Yavin Vassilika.]]
At some point, IG-88 would team up with [[Bossk/Legends|Bossk]] and [[Dengar/Legends|Dengar]], having been hired by the [[Hutt/Legends|Hutts]] to locate the [[Yavin Vassilika]]. Eventually, IG-88 turned on his teammates, attempting to claim a bounty on them which was recently posted by rival bounty hunter, [[Zuckuss/Legends|Zuckuss]].<ref name="Vassilika">''[[Star Wars: Underworld: The Yavin Vassilika]]''</ref>

After the Alliance's [[Renegade Squadron/Legends|Renegade Squadron]] caused a [[Battle of the Graveyard|stir]] in the Alderaan system, the Empire started actively hunting them. This led one of the IG-88s to pick up the bounty on the Squadron, finding them on Ord Mantell and [[Skirmish on Ord Mantell (0.5 ABY)|attempting]] to capture or kill all he could. However, due to the actions of [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]], they were able to temporarily defeat the droid and escape.<ref name="BF:RS">''[[Star Wars Battlefront: Renegade Squadron]]'' Mission 3</ref>

[[File:IG88_Unleashed.jpg|thumb|left|250px|IG-88 bounty hunting]]
In [[1 ABY/Legends|1 ABY]], IG-88 assisted [[Boba Fett/Legends|Boba Fett]] on a [[Battle of Circumtore|mission]] against the [[Shell Hutts]].<ref name="The Mandalorian Armor">''[[The Mandalorian Armor]]''</ref>

In [[3 ABY/Legends|3 ABY]], IG-88 was commissioned to find the [[Millennium Falcon/Legends|''Millennium Falcon'']]. However, IG-88 was beaten to the [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]] bounty by Boba Fett. IG-88B was destroyed on [[Bespin/Legends|Bespin]] by Fett in retaliation for attempting to track him. IG-88s C and D engaged Fett in orbit over [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]] in identical models of the [[IG-2000/Legends|''IG-2000'']] in attempt to steal the carbonite containing Solo, but were defeated. C was destroyed first. IG-88D then launched a surprise attack, but in the end its ship was also destroyed by Boba Fett's [[Slave I/Legends|''Slave I'']], in a maneuver in which Fett pretended to have been killed.<ref name="IG88 Tale" />

[[File:RendarsWrath .jpg|thumb|right|250px|IG-88 hunting Dash Rendar]]
Unbeknownst to Fett, IG-88D somehow survived the encounter, but was later [[Mission to Ord Mantell (Dash Rendar)|destroyed]] by [[Dash Rendar/Legends|Dash Rendar]] while looking for repair parts for his ship in an [[Ord Mantell/Legends|Ord Mantell]] junkyard while Rendar searched for information on the carbonite-frozen Han Solo.<ref>''[[Star Wars: Shadows of the Empire (video game)#Part II: In Search of Boba Fett]]''</ref>

At some point, one of the IG-88s came under the employment of the [[Zann Consortium/Legends|Zann Consortium]] criminal organization, apparently owing [[Urai Fen|the second-in-command]] of the organization a favor.<ref name="Star Wars: Empire at War: Forces of Corruption">''[[Star Wars: Empire at War: Forces of Corruption]]''</ref> He [[Ground Battle on Bespin|hacked]] into Bespin's central computer and retrieved information on the planets on Zann's "hit list".

Just before the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]], IG-88A was hired for one last mission. Vader hired the droid to deal with the Renegade Squadron once more, who had [[Battle of Sullust (4 ABY)|attacked]] Sullust in a diversionary attack. He was defeated again however, despite being equipped with a lightning-powered [[Deflector shield generator/Legends|shield generator]].

===Destruction over Endor===
[[File:IG-88B_SC.png|thumb|left|250px|IG-88B]]
The remaining IG-88 uploaded his consciousness into a computer core destined for [[Death Star II/Legends|Death Star II]]. He succeeded in being uploaded, and was preparing to activate his program to take over all droids in the galaxy when it was destroyed. With his consciousness in the Death Star II, he would literally ''become'' the Death Star.<ref name="IG88 Tale" />

[[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] was the only known person on the Death Star to suspect something was wrong after the uploading of the computer core with IG-88 inside. Before the station's destruction, he noticed a series of doors in his throne room opening and closing sporadically. IG-88 did this to show the Emperor that he was not all powerful. However, IG-88 was utterly baffled when it appeared that Emperor Palpatine used some [[The Force/Legends|unseen force]] to attempt to push the doors open. However, IG-88 exerted more force and was able to continue to keep the Emperor locked in, until he grew tired of the game and unlocked the door.<ref name="IG88 Tale" />

[[Lando Calrissian/Legends|Lando Calrissian]] and [[Wedge Antilles/Legends|Wedge Antilles]] ended up destroying the core, destroying both the Death Star, and the A.I. of IG-88 as well.

===Reactivation===
[[File:Raynar-kid.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Months after being reprogrammed, IG-88A, the last IG-88 droid, became a bodyguard of the Thul family.]]
Years later, the IG-88A body, now inactive, was reprogrammed. The droid worked for [[Barpotomous Drebble/Legends|Barpotomous Drebble]] temporarily in the months following the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]], and later was found in service to the [[House of Thul]], protecting them from the [[Diversity Alliance]] and serving as bodyguard of [[Tyko Thul]]. Later IG-88 would save the young [[Raynar Thul]] from near death, after being reprogrammed to protect the Thul family.<ref name="Young Jedi Knights: Delusions of Grandeur">''[[Young Jedi Knights: Delusions of Grandeur]]''</ref>

==Abilities and equipment==
IG-88's primary weapon was a [[BlasTech Industries/Legends|BlasTech]] [[DLT-20A blaster rifle/Legends|DLT-20A blaster rifle]]. Other weapons included the following:
*[[Flamethrower/Legends|Flamethrower]]<ref name="SWCVD" />

*[[Scomp link/Legends|Computer input port]]

*Heat and motion sensors<ref name="SWCVD" />
*Highly advanced trackers
*Acid-proof servo wires<ref name="SWCVD" />
*Armor nearly impenetrable from external attack
*Cutting laser in finger on right arm
*''Extremely'' fast reflexes, even by droid standards; during his escape, the droid managed to kill a technician by calmly and methodically calculating the trajectory of an incoming laser bolt, deciding to deflect the bolt instead of dodging it, and furthermore making sure that his deflected beam reflected at just the right angle to kill the fleeing technician who had fired upon him -all in the microseconds that it took the laser bolt to travel from the gun to his position.
*Extreme physical strength.
*As the Second Death Star, IG-88A possessed all the armaments and capabilities of the station itself, including, most notably, its planet-destroying superlaser.
*Superheated Armor-Plating
[[File:IG-2000-FF78.png|thumb|left|300px|IG-88A piloted ''IG-2000''.]]
IG-88 was designed to have blaster cannons built into the structure of each arm, but that they were not yet installed.<ref name="IG88 Tale" /> IG-88 used external weapons for the rest of his existence, indicating that they were never installed later.

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|IG-88 is so much shorter than I thought, lol!|A [[Star Wars: Tiny Death Star|bitizen]] through the HoloNet feed|<ref name="Star Wars: Tiny Death Star">''[[Star Wars: Tiny Death Star]]''</ref>}}
IG-88 seems to be primarily built from parts of aircraft scrap, though most of his parts have yet to be identified. The droid's head was constructed from a Rolls-Royce Derwent jet engine burner can with slight modifications and additions. Similar burner cans were originally used as part of the distillery behind the bar in the Mos Eisley Cantina in [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''A New Hope'']]. A similar prop also appears in a junkyard in "Dawn of the Gods", an episode of the British science-fiction series [[Wikipedia:Blake's 7|''Blake's 7'']] which aired in 1980.<ref name="Atomic Donkey">{{Blogspot|subdomain=bsmbow|url=2009/11/bounty-hunter-ig-88-in-blakes-7.html|name=Atomic Donkey #0|text=Bounty Hunter IG-88 in Blake's 7}}</ref>

According to the ''Shadows of the Empire'' PC video game, IG-88 speaks in a deep, mechanical, almost Vader-esque tone as opposed to the more differently pitched voices presented by the battle droids of the Prequel trilogy.

[[File:IG88_concept_btm.jpg|thumb|right|250px|IG-88 concept art&mdash;Referred to in production as the "chrome war droid"]]
IG-88's gun included modifications, including the addition of six grips around the barrel. The exact identity of the grip material has yet to be determined, but recent revelations suggest stamped metal T-track from old cupboards with sliding doors for the ''A New Hope'' grips. The grips on ''The Empire Strikes Back'' lightsabers are rubber or plastic and may be newer style T-track or reproductions of the original ANH grips. It is unknown at this time if ''The Empire Strikes Back'' E-11 blasters had the original ANH grip material or newer grips of plastic or rubber. Note: The row of holes on the underside of the gun had no grips as they would interfere with the folding stock. Also, the row of holes just above the folding stock the left side of the gun received no grips, presumably this is because of the bayonet attachment stub that occupies the third hole from the front in this row.

Another modification includes the addition of a M19 or M32 azimuth scope (see below) to a mount by the use of the two hex head bolts that came with the scope. This scope mount is in the form of an approximately 1&#32;cm wide by 1/16" - 1/8" thick strip of metal sitting about a 1/4" above the gun. The front end of the strip was bent and inserted into the rear most vent hole on the top of the gun thus requiring no rivet or other attachment. On this blaster variation the rear of the mount strip goes straight back into the rear sight and is attached there presumably by riveting it to the sight.

An IG-88 body, presumably IG-88B's, is seen on Bespin in the scene where [[Chewbacca/Legends|Chewbacca]] is recovering the parts of [[C-3PO/Legends|C-3PO]] from the [[Ugnaught/Legends|Ugnaughts]].

In ''[[LEGO Star Wars II: The Original Trilogy]]'' IG-88 is playable in Free Play mode.
Also, IG-88 is available in free play in ''[[LEGO Star Wars: The Complete Saga]]''.
In a possible oversight by the designers, IG-88 is playable in the final battle of ''[[Star Wars: Empire at War: Forces of Corruption]]'', whereas all four IG-88s would have been destroyed by that point.

Rapper MC Chris wrote a track on his Part Six Part One album about IG-88 called "IG-88's '57 Chevy".

In the computer game ''Half-Life: Opposing Force'', a security guard can be heard saying 'Have you seen the new IG-88?' Shortly before being killed.

The timed-explosive device used by an assassin in the Episode "Chuck Versus the Third Dimension" of the TV show "Chuck", has the designation IG-88.

In the book [[Wikipedia:Scarecrow (novel)|''Scarecrow'']] by Matthew Reilly, one of the bounty hunting groups calls itself the Intercontinental Guard, Unit 88 or IG-88.
